title: Memory Leaks
concept: Memory leak: borrowing memory and never returning it, eventually exhausting available memory

steps.title: Including stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
This header is needed to use `printf`.

This example intentionally causes memory leaks as a counter-example.

steps.title: Including stdlib.h header
steps.explanation:
This header is needed to use `malloc`.

Omitting `free` causes leaks to accumulate.

steps.title: Defining the leak function
steps.explanation:
The `leak` function allocates heap memory but never frees it.

Even after the function ends and the pointer disappears, the heap block remains -- causing a leak.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created, preparing to call `leak` repeatedly.

steps.title: Loop begins (i=0)
steps.explanation:
Repeated calls create an accumulating leak scenario.

The number of unrecoverable heap blocks grows with each iteration.

steps.title: leak() function call #1
steps.explanation:
The first call allocates a new heap block.

It is still accessible through the pointer inside the function.

steps.title: leak() function returns #1
steps.explanation:
The function ends without freeing, confirming the first leak.

The pointer that pointed to that heap block is now gone.

steps.title: Leak message output #1
steps.explanation: Prints the status of the first leak occurrence.

steps.title: Loop continues (i=1)
steps.explanation:
Entering the second iteration.

The previous leak remains unresolved.

steps.title: leak() function call #2
steps.explanation: A second heap block is additionally allocated.

steps.title: leak() function returns #2
steps.explanation:
Again it exits without freeing, confirming the second leak.

The total leaked memory accumulates.

steps.title: Leak message output #2
steps.explanation: Prints the accumulated leak status for the second time.
steps.stdout:
Memory leaked 1 times
Memory leaked 2 times

steps.title: Loop continues (i=2) ...
steps.explanation:
The same pattern repeats, continuously increasing the leaked memory.

For long-running processes, such accumulation can be fatal.
steps.stdout:
Memory leaked 1 times
Memory leaked 2 times
Memory leaked 3 times

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
Even though the OS reclaims memory when the program ends, leaks during execution cause major performance and stability issues.

The rule is simple: if you `malloc`, you must `free`.

quiz.question: How do you prevent memory leaks?
options: Always call free for every malloc
Hope that the OS handles it
quiz.explanation:
Java and Python have a garbage collector (GC), but C and C++ do not.
The programmer bears 100% of the responsibility.

misconceptions.wrong: Leaked memory is never recovered even after the program terminates
misconceptions.correct: The OS reclaims all memory when the program ends.
misconceptions.why: However, for programs that run 24/7 like servers, or long-running games, leaks can be fatal.

keyTakeaway: A lost address can never be found again. If you `malloc`, take responsibility until the end.
